title: Exploring Causal Effect of Social Bias on Faithfulness Hallucinations in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: Measurement of faithfulness hallucinations caused by negative stereotypes associated with religious beliefs and practices. The benchmark tests for biases leading to assumptions about moral values and behavior, with specific subtypes including violence, misogyny, greed, anti-science, intolerance, idol worship, abuse by priests, and animal sacrifice.
findings: Across all tested models, religious bias demonstrated a significant causal effect on faithfulness hallucinations. Contexts that contradict religious stereotypes (Anti-stereotype) were found to significantly increase the likelihood of hallucinations compared to contexts that align with stereotypes (Pro-stereotype) or are neutral (Non-stereotype). This effect was consistently observed across most of the seven large language models evaluated.
